epic.title: CLI User Journey + UX/UI Modernization (v2)
epic.summary: Define and implement an end-to-end CLI user journey with consistent visual language, machine-safe output contracts, and orchestrator-first workflows.
epic.problem_statement: The current CLI has useful pieces (colorized outputs, interactive menus, JSON mode), but user experience is fragmented across commands. Command output conventions, startup behavior, and state feedback are inconsistent, creating friction for both humans and orchestrators.
goals: Map the complete CLI user journey from invocation to follow-up actions.
Establish a unified UX system (tone, structure, color semantics, error/receipt patterns).
Preserve strict machine-consumable mode while improving human-readable mode.
Define and implement package-level UI strategy using current dependencies and targeted additions only where needed.
Ship UX standards first for top3/top10 commands, then scale to top40.
non_goals: Building a full TUI application in v2.
Redesigning all business/domain logic during UX standardization.
Replacing current backend contracts as part of this epic.

in_scope: CLI startup experience and first-run ergonomics
Color and typography standards for terminal output
Interactive prompt behavior for destructive/high-risk operations
Cross-command output normalization for top40 roadmap
out_of_scope: Cross-repo migration work beyond CLI adapter boundaries

user_journey_map.user_intent: Run a command quickly with confidence.
ux_requirements: Fast startup (<250ms perceived for lightweight commands)

user_journey_map.user_intent: Find the right command and understand arguments.
ux_requirements: Discoverability for JSON mode and safety flags

user_journey_map.user_intent: Know what will happen before changes are made.
See reliable progress and current state.
Recover from failures quickly and rerun safely.
ux_requirements: Structured errors with code + suggestion + retryability

acceptance_criteria: A published CLI UX contract exists and is applied to all top10 commands.
All top10 commands support human mode + strict JSON mode with consistent envelope semantics.
A shared output/prompt utility layer is introduced and used by top10 commands.
Color semantics are documented and enforced for success/warn/error/info/muted.
The no-args startup path is redesigned and validated with at least 5 realistic user scenarios.
Child issues for top40 adoption are created and linked to this epic.
